ana: Heads-up — AuroraSys wants a joint performance sweep next week. Goal: perf/W and sustained throughput across our 8-bit quantized stack + kernel knob tuning. They want a public-friendly chart and an internal perf playbook. Can we draft a run playlist and ownership?
suresh: I can own kernel knobs + telemetry. Need to confirm hardware SKUs and power measurement rig. Do we have exact cards & firmware?
emily: I'll own workloads + datasets. Propose LLaMA-7B quant eval + a small real-customer prompt set (50 prompts). Want to include both streaming latency and 99th percentile tail.
michael: pinging infra — what capacity needed? rough estimate: 5x machines, each 4 GPUs, 4 runs per day for 3 days -> ~60 GPU-days.

suresh: For power telemetry we'll use the inline wattmeter + Prometheus exporter. Need list of metrics: package_power, vrm_power, ambient_temp, fan_rpm, pkts_dropped. Also add GPU_util, mem_util, adc_temp.
emily: Dataset list: 50 customer prompts (sanitized), 1000 tokens synthetic long-form (seq=2048), 200 short prompts for latency. We'll capture token-level timings and token counts.
suresh: Recommend kernel knob sweep: 
```
export KERNEL_TILES=(32 64 128 256)
export PREFETCH=(on off)
export MEMPOOL=(default pinned)
for t in "${KERNEL_TILES[@]}"; do for p in "${PREFETCH[@]}"; do for m in "${MEMPOOL[@]}"; do \n  run_sweep --model redwood-8q --tile $t --prefetch $p --mempool $m --batch 1,2,4 --seq 512,1024,2048 \n  # logs -> /mnt/bench/results/$t-$p-$m
done; done; done
```
This will produce ~72 combinations * batches * seqs. Expect ~300 total jobs.
emily: We'll also run an A/B against their tuned kernel branch and our baseline. Need a simple naming convention: partner/AURORA, redwood/Baseline.
suresh: Agree on naming. Also add a quick smoke that validates numerical parity on 100 samples before running large sweeps.

emily: Can we include a short public-friendly chart? I'd like perf/W vs throughput across knobs, and an inset comparing latency tail. Marketing wants a simplified caption.
suresh: We'll export perf/W as Joules-per-token and throughput as tok/s. For charting: x-axis throughput (tok/s), y-axis perf/W (tok/J), color by knob set. Keep legend simple.
